title: Are we there yet? A reality check on six big tech promises
gist: Index page for MIT Technology Review's 'Are we there yet?' package, which scores six long-promised technologies on a 0-10 progress meter. It lists the six topics but gives no scores itself.

insights.claim: MIT Technology Review ran progress reports on six technologies long 'just around the corner' and scored each on a 0-to-10 meter, where 0 means 'we don't even know where to begin' and 10 means 'we did it'.
insights.speaker: MIT Technology Review
insights.so_what: Gives a simple readiness rubric for comparing hype across unrelated fields.

insights.claim: The six technologies are nuclear-powered spaceships, exercise in a pill, interspecies communication, solid-state batteries, cleaning up PFAS and eliminating traffic deaths.
insights.speaker: MIT Technology Review
insights.so_what: Only solid-state batteries and PFAS cleanup have obvious near-term investable supply chains.

insights.claim: Eliminating traffic deaths is framed as achievable with simple, proven road-safety methods that could save more than 1 million lives worldwide each year.
insights.speaker: MIT Technology Review
insights.so_what: Unlike the other five, this problem is described as one of deployment rather than invention.
insights.quote: could save more than 1 million lives worldwide each year
